questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Democratic vs Non-Democratic Outcomes' refers to.
questions.a: Democracies differ from non-democratic regimes in how they produce outcomes: democracies are based on political competition, free elections and accountability, while non-democratic regimes concentrate power and lack such mechanisms.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democratic vs Non-Democratic Outcomes'.
questions.a: The difference between democracy and non-democracy is best judged by examining the actual outcomes each produces for the people.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Democratic vs Non-Democratic Outcomes'.
questions.a: How do democratic outcomes differ from non-democratic outcomes?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Accountability and Transparency in Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Accountability means that elected rulers are answerable to the people for their actions and decisions, while transparency means that the processes of decision-making are open to public scrutiny.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Accountability and Transparency in Democracy'.
questions.a: Democracy ensures that decision-makers are accountable to the people and that decision-making is transparent.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Accountability and Transparency in Democracy'.
questions.a: What is accountability in a democracy?

concepts.title: Economic Growth and Development under Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic Growth and Development under Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Economic growth refers to the increase in a country's total income and output over time. Democracies have not been consistently better at economic growth compared to dictatorships, as decisions are often delayed by consultation and negotiation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic Growth and Development under Democracy'.
questions.a: Democracy may be slower in economic decision-making, so its record on economic growth is mixed when compared with non-democratic regimes.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Economic Growth and Development under Democracy'.
questions.a: How does democracy affect economic growth?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic Equality under Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Economic inequality refers to the gap in income and wealth between the rich and the poor. Democracies are based on political equality but have not been very successful in reducing economic inequalities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic Equality under Democracy'.
questions.a: Democracy provides political equality (one person, one vote) but has a mixed record on reducing economic inequality.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Economic Equality under Democracy'.
questions.a: How far does democracy reduce economic inequality?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dignity and Freedom of Citizens' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy stands much superior to any non-democratic regime in promoting the dignity and freedom of the individual, including the freedom of women and disadvantaged groups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dignity and Freedom of Citizens'.
questions.a: Democracy enhances the dignity and freedom of citizens, especially of women and marginalised groups.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Dignity and Freedom of Citizens'.
questions.a: How does democracy promote the dignity and freedom of citizens?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reduction of Inequality and Discrimination' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy helps reduce discrimination and inequality by giving every citizen an equal vote and by allowing disadvantaged groups to organise and demand their rights.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reduction of Inequality and Discrimination'.
questions.a: Democracy provides a platform for disadvantaged groups to fight discrimination and demand equality.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Reduction of Inequality and Discrimination'.
questions.a: How does democracy help reduce discrimination?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Comparison of Democracies' refers to.
questions.a: When we compare democracies with non-democracies on various outcomes, democracy is better on accountability, dignity and freedom, but its record on economic growth and equality is mixed.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Comparison of Democracies'.
questions.a: Democracy is not a guarantee of economic success, but it is clearly better on political and social outcomes.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Comparison of Democracies'.
questions.a: Compare democracies and non-democracies on economic outcomes.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Quality of Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: The quality of a democracy depends on the participation of citizens, the openness of decision-making, and the extent to which it delivers on the expectations of the people. A good democracy is one that is accountable, transparent and responsive.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Quality of Democracy'.
questions.a: A high-quality democracy is one where citizens participate actively and the government is accountable, transparent and responsive.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Quality of Democracy'.
questions.a: What determines the quality of a democracy?
